items.b: NINE FORTY AT THE EXCHANGE, THIRTEEN TWELVE AT THE COUNTER
items.t: — The Shanghai Gold Exchange closed Au99.99 at 940.72 yuan a gram today, from an opening of 955.00 and a session low of 933.01, on 3,886.14 kilogrammes; Au(T+D) closed at 940.44 on 41,646 kilogrammes. Those are the exchange's own published quotations, not an aggregator's copy. On the same day Chow Tai Fook listed 24-carat jewellery at 1,312 yuan a gram, carried identically by two independent Chinese aggregators, jinjia.com.cn and cngold. That puts the counter 39.47% above the exchange, a gap of 371.28 yuan a gram, this desk's arithmetic. This paper published the same pair on 9 August at 938 and 1,286, a gap of 348 yuan and a markup of 37.10%. Six days on, the exchange has moved 0.29% and the counter 2.02%: the gap did not close, it widened by 23.28 yuan a gram

items.b: THE COUNTER CUT TWICE AS FAST AS THE METAL
items.t: — Today both legs fell and they fell at very different speeds. The exchange closed 8.52 yuan below its 13 August close of 949.24, a fall of 0.90%. The Chow Tai Fook counter came off 28 yuan from 1,340, a fall of 2.09%, roughly two and a third times as fast. The premium therefore narrowed today, from 41.17% on one aggregator's 13 August counter price or 40.01% on the other's, to 39.47%. The counter moves in steps and the exchange moves in fractions: this month the brand price has gone 1,231, 1,240, 1,297, 1,286, 1,308, 1,308, 1,336, 1,329, 1,340 and 1,312, round jumps of tens of yuan against an exchange that rarely moves one per cent in a day. On the readings this desk can verify, the Chinese jewellery markup has run between 37.10% and 41.17% in August. A listed counter price is an asking price, not a transacted one, and workmanship charges and store discounts sit outside both numbers

items.b: OUTSIDE SOURCES DISAGREE ON THE CHINESE COUNTER, AND IT IS DISCLOSED
items.t: — Two disclosures belong with the figures above. One aggregator's series carries 1,286 against 7 August rather than the 8 August this paper published it under, and the same two aggregators disagree about 13 August by 11 yuan, one reading 1,340 and the other 1,329. This desk cannot establish which board hour either page is reading and does not resolve it here. The 14 August counter price of 1,312 is the one both pages agree on, which is why today's comparison is anchored there rather than on the disputed day. Separately, the Bank of China's market note of 13 August put Shanghai spot gold up 0.96% at 955.75 yuan a gram, where the exchange's own daily quotation for that date closes Au99.99 at 949.24. The exchange's own figure is the one used here. Divergence between outside sources is always disclosed; that rule is untouched

— Kitco's live board at 06:00 New York time read gold $4,356.20, silver $64.77, platinum $1,725.00 and palladium $1,297.00, and all four are written back over caratwire's 04:59 marks with the source named and the timestamp new. Against this paper's own marks 24 hours earlier: gold down $27.90 or 0.64%, silver up $0.25 or 0.39%, platinum up $15.00 or 0.88%, palladium down $22.00 or 1.67%. Gold and silver were checked against TradingEconomics at $4,356.79 and $64.89, 0.01% and 0.19% away. Platinum had been held twice, on 12 August for a stale cell and on 13 August because Kitco sat $14.60 below two pages that agreed with each other. At 04:59 today the tape desk found the same shape a third time and held again. At 06:00 the gap is $12.70 against TradingEconomics at $1,737.70 and $14.90 against JM Bullion at $1,739.90, with those two agreeing to $2.20, or 0.13%

items.b: WHY THE MARK WAS TAKEN RATHER THAN HELD A THIRD TIME
items.t: — Three mornings of the same gap in the same direction, at the same order of magnitude, reads as a basis difference between outside pages rather than as a market nobody can read. Treating it as the second thing had a cost: the held mark of $1,710.00 was two sessions old and 1.62% below where two other pages put the metal, which is a stale number wearing the protection of good procedure. Platinum is therefore written back on Kitco, the board that carries every other mark on this tape, and palladium with it at Kitco's $1,297.00 bid. JM Bullion read palladium at $1,336.71 at 06:01, $39.71 or 3.06% higher, which on a metal this thin is the other side of a spread rather than a disagreement about the price. Leaving one Kitco mark frozen and three Kitco marks fresh, from the same board at the same minute, is the two-numbers problem the one-price rule exists to remove. A jeweller quoting platinum off a single public board this morning is choosing between $1,725.00 and $1,739.90 without being told there is a choice

items.b: SEVENTY-ONE MILLION FROM AMERICA IN A THREE BILLION DOLLAR MONTH
items.t: — Global gold-backed ETFs took in $3 billion in July, reversing two consecutive months of outflows, in figures the World Gold Council published on 6 August under the title Europe's golden heatwave. Collective holdings rose 23 tonnes to 4,068 tonnes and assets under management rose 1% to $530 billion. Europe took $2 billion of it, the United Kingdom alone $875 million and Switzerland $657 million. Asia took $616 million, with China strongest and Japan in outflow. North America took $71 million. Other regions took $140 million. Britain and Switzerland together raised $1,532 million against $827 million from everywhere outside Europe, a ratio of 1.85 to one and this desk's arithmetic; North America, the largest gold ETF market in the world by assets, supplied 2.5% of the named regional total. The named regions sum to $2,827 million against a rounded headline of $3 billion because every component is rounded, and that subtraction is this desk's. The figures are eight days old as they print, and this paper has cited the World Gold Council fifteen times without ever covering its flows series

— The Bureau ranked the ETF item first and this desk moved it to third after confirming the publication date, which is 6 August and eight days back; a monthly research report that old is reported honestly rather than led with. The Bureau's second item, Shanghai gold with a Chow Tai Fook counter at 1,340 yuan described as closing the wholesale-retail gap, ran as the lead with both halves corrected: 1,340 is one aggregator's 13 August figure and the other reads 1,329, and on this paper's own arithmetic the gap has widened since 8 August rather than closed. The gold-to-silver ratio piece the Bureau offered as optional filler is not run as an article; the ratio at 67.26, narrowing 0.69 points from 67.95, appears inside the tape story instead. Two items were verified and dropped: Tenoris's US jewellery half-year, which is dated 9 July and which this paper has already covered nine times including on 8 August, and Sotheby's Gem Drop August, whose sale closed in New York yesterday and whose own results page still carries no total
